project.name: 9routerx
project.description: One command, multi-provider AI gateway, everywhere. 9routerx installs and manages Claude Code, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor IDE, and 9router on local machines and VPS hosts.

nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: GitHub Actions workflow that lints shell scripts, checks shell, Python, and Worker syntax, and runs functional contract checks on pushes and pull requests to master. Version tags create a GitHub release only after all validation jobs succeed.
nodes.languageNotes: The release job uses GitHub Actions job dependencies and a tag predicate to gate changelog-backed releases on all validation jobs.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: Tracks the 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 releases, including remote VPS installation, universal-installer improvements, Cloudflare Worker routes, health tooling, and shell fixes.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Provides repository development guidance covering installation and health commands, combo management, Cloudflare Worker deployment, component architecture, data flow, implementation constraints, and troubleshooting.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Explains the one-command local and VPS installation flow for the multi-provider AI gateway, including health checks, virtual model combos, Cloudflare Worker deployment, release operations, troubleshooting, and API-key security.

nodes.name: install-universal.sh
nodes.summary: Acts as the POSIX shell bootstrap entry point: it selects the latest release, downloads required and optional 9routerx scripts into ~/.9routerx using atomic temporary files, sets executable permissions, and hands control to the core installer.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses POSIX sh with set -eu and an atomic mktemp-then-mv download pattern restricted to HTTPS.

nodes.name: safe_download
nodes.summary: Downloads one installer asset to a temporary sibling file, verifies that it is non-empty, atomically moves it into place, and cleans up while reporting failures.

nodes.name: wrangler.toml
nodes.summary: Configures the 9routerx Cloudflare Worker deployment with worker.js as its entry point and a 2024-01-01 compatibility date.

nodes.name: bootstrap-vps.sh
nodes.summary: Thin VPS bootstrap entry point that resolves its sibling installer and replaces the current process with install.sh in non-interactive vps-headless mode.

nodes.name: doctor.sh
nodes.summary: Diagnoses local Cursor and headless VPS installations by checking required tools, 9router health, client routing configuration, and Linux service persistence, with optional remediation for server failures.
nodes.languageNotes: Strict-mode Bash uses shared issue flags to separate diagnosis from remediation and embeds Python for JSON configuration inspection.

nodes.name: tty_read
nodes.summary: Reads an interactive value from /dev/tty when available, otherwise falls back to standard input, and applies the supplied default for empty input.

nodes.name: usage
nodes.summary: Prints command-line help for selecting a diagnostic mode and enabling interactive or unattended remediation.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Parses doctor mode, fix, yes, and help flags while rejecting unknown options.

nodes.name: choose_mode_if_needed
nodes.summary: Requires or interactively chooses between local Cursor and headless VPS diagnostics, refusing ambiguous non-TTY execution.

nodes.name: check_9router_process
nodes.summary: Locates the 9router executable, checks for a matching running process, and records whether startup remediation is required.

nodes.name: check_systemd_service
nodes.summary: Checks Linux systemd availability plus the 9router unit active and enabled states, then records install or restart remediation flags.

nodes.name: check_common
nodes.summary: Runs shared binary, database, process, HTTP, IPv4/localhost, and Linux service checks used by every diagnostic mode.

nodes.name: check_local_cursor
nodes.summary: Checks for the Cursor CLI and for a signed-in Cursor state database across macOS and Linux locations.

nodes.name: check_client_config
nodes.summary: Validates Claude Code, shell, and Cursor routing settings, warns about insecure dummy tokens on public endpoints, and probes the configured 9router address.

nodes.name: check_vps_headless
nodes.summary: Checks both case variants of the headless Cursor state database path and reports recent 9router startup log entries.

nodes.name: run_fix
nodes.summary: Confirms and applies server remediations by installing or restarting a systemd unit, falling back to nohup, and polling the gateway for recovery.

nodes.name: print_summary
nodes.summary: Prints accumulated pass, warning, and failure counts for the diagnostic run.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Coordinates argument parsing, mode-specific checks, summary reporting, and optional headless remediation before returning a failing status for unresolved checks.

nodes.name: generate-api-key.sh
nodes.summary: Connects to a remote VPS over SSH, creates a scoped 9router API key through the loopback API, enables login enforcement, and prints the token with a Claude Code configuration example.
nodes.languageNotes: A quoted heredoc sends a strict-mode shell program over SSH so administrative API calls remain bound to the remote loopback interface.

nodes.name: install.sh
nodes.summary: Primary installer and cleanup orchestrator for local Cursor, headless Linux, and remote VPS workflows; it installs AI tooling, initializes state, manages 9router services and cron, and synchronizes Cursor credentials over SSH.
nodes.languageNotes: The Bash workflow embeds Python for SQLite and JSON mutations and reuses one SSH ControlMaster connection during remote installation and verification.

nodes.name: banner
nodes.summary: Prints the branded 9routerx installer banner and product description.

nodes.name: tty_read
nodes.summary: Reads a prompt response from /dev/tty or standard input and returns the configured default when no value is entered.

nodes.name: usage
nodes.summary: Prints documented switches for local, headless, and remote-token synchronization workflows.

nodes.name: parse_args
nodes.summary: Parses install, remote sync, Cursor, and uninstall options into the installer workflow state and rejects unknown flags.

nodes.name: choose_mode_if_needed
nodes.summary: Prompts for an installation, remote synchronization, or cleanup workflow and maps local installation to an OS-appropriate mode.

nodes.name: resolve_mode
nodes.summary: Resolves interactive or compatibility mode selection and validates the final workflow against the supported installer modes.

nodes.name: npm_global_install
nodes.summary: Installs a global npm package through a writable prefix, root, sudo, or a user-local macOS prefix according to current permissions.

nodes.name: install_homebrew
nodes.summary: Installs Homebrew when absent, loads the discovered shell environment, and confirms availability.

nodes.name: install_node_if_missing
nodes.summary: Keeps an existing Node.js/npm pair or installs it through Homebrew, apt, dnf, or yum for the detected operating system.

nodes.name: npm_pkg_outdated
nodes.summary: Compares a globally installed npm package version with the registry version, treating missing packages as outdated and lookup failures as current.

nodes.name: install_or_update_npm_pkg
nodes.summary: Installs a missing global npm command or upgrades its backing package when the registry reports a newer version.

nodes.name: install_claude_code
nodes.summary: Updates an existing Claude Code installation or installs it through the official native installer.

nodes.name: install_antigravity
nodes.summary: Installs or updates the global antigravity-ide npm package based on command and registry state.

nodes.name: install_copilot_cli
nodes.summary: Installs or upgrades GitHub Copilot through the gh extension when possible, with the npm CLI as a fallback.

nodes.name: install_cursor
nodes.summary: Honors the Cursor install policy, keeps an existing CLI, installs the macOS cask, or gives Linux download guidance.

nodes.name: install_9routerx_cli
nodes.summary: Copies the repository 9routerx launcher into the user-local bin directory and warns when that directory is absent from PATH.

nodes.name: install_auto_update_cron
nodes.summary: Locates the bundled auto-update scripts, asks for consent in a TTY, and invokes the cron installer with the 9router log path.

nodes.name: init_cursor_state_db_headless
nodes.summary: Creates both Linux Cursor state database path variants and optionally seeds access, refresh, and email authentication values from the environment.

nodes.name: init_9router_db
nodes.summary: Creates the initial 9router JSON database with empty provider data and explicit gateway, observability, routing, and authentication defaults.

nodes.name: _wait_for_9router
nodes.summary: Polls the local providers endpoint for up to ten attempts to determine whether 9router is ready.

nodes.name: _install_systemd_service
nodes.summary: Writes and enables a hardened 9router systemd unit with restart policy, noninteractive input, and persistent log output.

nodes.name: start_9router_daemon
nodes.summary: Starts 9router on Linux through systemd when available or nohup otherwise, then waits for the local gateway endpoint to become ready.

nodes.name: read_cursor_auth_from_db
nodes.summary: Uses embedded Python to locate the Cursor SQLite state database and emit required access, refresh, email, and machine identity values.

nodes.name: remote_vps_install
nodes.summary: Maintains one SSH control connection while uploading and running the headless installer, synchronizing Cursor credentials, registering the provider, and remotely verifying or repairing the result.

nodes.name: uninstall
nodes.summary: Performs scoped configuration, service/data, and tool cleanup with interactive or flag-driven confirmation, dry-run support, and optional Claude removal.

nodes.name: print_local_summary
nodes.summary: Prints local or headless quick-start commands and the appropriate 9router dashboard address after installation.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Dispatches remote sync and uninstall modes or performs the full local/headless dependency, state, daemon, cron, and completion workflow.

nodes.name: install_auto_update_cron.sh
nodes.summary: Idempotently installs or replaces a daily cron entry for auto-update.py, spreading execution across a stable machine-derived time and appending output to the configured log.
nodes.languageNotes: The schedule hashes an optional machine ID to reduce simultaneous update traffic while retaining a deterministic fallback time.

nodes.name: 9routerx
nodes.summary: Provides the top-level 9routerx command, dispatching model browsing, interactive combo management, and safe auto-update operations to the bundled Python utilities.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash dispatches subcommands while embedded Python handles grouping and validated interactive model selection.

nodes.name: usage
nodes.summary: Prints the supported 9routerx commands and the environment variable used to select the router API.

nodes.name: _find_auto_update_py

nodes.name: _find_auto_update_cron_sh

nodes.name: auto_update

nodes.name: _is_idle

nodes.name: _restart_service

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Coordinates version checks, idle gating, global npm installation, and service restart for one updater run.

nodes.languageNotes: JSON mutations are persisted atomically through a temporary file and os.replace.

nodes.name: utc_now_iso

nodes.name: read_json

nodes.name: write_json

nodes.name: http_json

nodes.name: fetch_models

nodes.name: ensure_db_shape

nodes.name: normalize_strategy

nodes.name: cmd_list

nodes.name: cmd_create

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: README.md introduces 9routerx as a one-command, multi-provider AI gateway setup for local machines and VPS hosts. It also maps the health, model-combo, edge-delivery, release, troubleshooting, and API-key concepts that the remaining steps connect into an operating system.

tour.title: Edge Installer Route
tour.description: worker.js is the public edge entry point, serving installer and bootstrap scripts while selecting the latest GitHub release when one is available. wrangler.toml binds that script as the Cloudflare Worker deployment entry, showing how the one-command flow begins before code runs on the target machine.
tour.languageLesson: Wrangler configuration keeps Cloudflare deployment metadata separate from the JavaScript request handler, so routing code and platform settings can evolve independently.

tour.title: Universal Bootstrap
tour.description: After the edge route delivers the bootstrap, install-universal.sh selects a release and downloads the required and optional scripts into ~/.9routerx. It uses temporary files, applies executable permissions, and then hands control to the core installer, creating a stable bridge from the public command to versioned release content.
tour.languageLesson: A POSIX shell bootstrap can make downloads atomic by writing temporary files before exposing them as executable commands, preventing partial transfers from replacing a usable installer.

tour.title: Core Installation Paths
tour.description: install.sh is the topology's broadest file and orchestrates local Cursor, headless Linux, and remote VPS installation as well as cleanup. bootstrap-vps.sh depends on it and replaces its own process with the installer in non-interactive vps-headless mode, keeping the VPS entry point thin while centralizing behavior in one implementation.
tour.languageLesson: Shell exec replaces the bootstrap process rather than spawning a child, so signals and the final exit status belong directly to the real installer.

tour.title: Gateway Commands and Combos
tour.description: Once installation is complete, the 9routerx command becomes the operator-facing control surface for model browsing, combo management, and safe updates. Its direct dependency on combo.py leads to the persisted virtual-model workflows, where users can list, create, test, and delete fallback or round-robin combinations.

tour.title: Lifecycle Updates
tour.description: The topology connects initial setup and daily operation to two maintenance components: install.sh depends on the cron installer, while the 9routerx command depends on auto-update.py. The cron script installs a stable machine-derived daily schedule, and the updater waits for an hour of idle proxy traffic before upgrading the package and restarting its service. Together they keep the gateway current without treating active requests as an acceptable interruption window.

tour.title: Credential Provisioning and Sync
tour.description: For a remote gateway, generate-api-key.sh creates a scoped key through the VPS loopback API, enables login enforcement, and emits client configuration guidance. The sync utility then discovers and probes default models or server-defined combos before updating Claude Code, Cursor, and shell profiles; the core installer ties this into its SSH-based credential synchronization path.

tour.title: Health Checks and Repair
tour.description: The installer depends on doctor.sh to verify the system it has assembled rather than assuming setup succeeded. The diagnostic path checks prerequisites, gateway health, client routing, and Linux service persistence, and it can remediate server failures when requested. This closes the operational loop between installation, synchronized credentials, and a reachable gateway.

tour.title: Release Delivery Loop
tour.description: The GitHub Actions pipeline validates shell, Python, Worker, and functional contracts, then permits version tags to create releases only after those checks pass. CHANGELOG.md records installer, edge-route, health, and lifecycle changes, while worker.js resolves the latest release for new bootstrap requests. This capstone connects validated repository changes back to the same edge delivery route where the tour's runtime path began.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions uses job dependencies and tag predicates to make release publication conditional on earlier validation jobs rather than merely on the presence of a version tag.
